sources.title: OSS Personnel Files from Excel
sources.locator: PDF page 115, printed rows 43-46, and page 116, printed rows 2-6; both complete pages rendered and visually checked; Box 183, 230/86/30/01
sources.collection_name: Records of the Office of Strategic Services, Record Group 226
sources.rights_notes: Nine printed rows remain separate. Protected service identifiers stay in private SQLite; the shared identifier in the two Deull rows is described but never reproduced in this bundle. Harold C Deutsch, already researched, is the intervening page-116 row and is not overwritten.

sources.title: Electronic Army Serial Number Merged File, ca. 1938-1946
sources.author_creator: Adjutant General's Office; National Personnel Records Center; National Archives and Records Administration
sources.locator: Official unrestricted bulk file ASNEF.FIN.DAT; complete 9,200,232-record scan; private identifier comparisons for five cohort index rows
sources.collection_name: Records of the National Archives and Records Administration, Record Group 64
sources.rights_notes: Exact private identifiers are omitted from this reviewed bundle and public outputs. Army-entry civilian occupation codes do not identify a named employer or an immediate pre-OSS affiliation. No Catalog API response was retained.

sources.title: Catherine Devaney Wallace, 87, Longtime Fairfield Resident
sources.locator: Obituary paragraph describing Rhode Island College and wartime OSS recruitment; full article reviewed
sources.rights_notes: The account explicitly places college attendance before OSS recruitment. It also names two workplaces without dating them; neither is assigned as a pre-OSS employer. Family details are excluded.

claims.claim_text: The indexed William C Deutsch is a high-confidence match to the William C Deutsch in the official Army enlistment file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The independent Army bulk record agrees on full indexed name and a protected identifier that is not shared by another index person.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an exact full-name and private identifier agreement across two official records; the OSS personnel file itself is unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Army entry predates wartime OSS service, but the entry does not name a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The full service identifier remains private; an Army occupation code is not treated as an employer.

claims.claim_text: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army record supports identity, but its coded occupation field does not name an employer, and the 1919 newspaper-page discovery lead lacks an inspected identity bridge.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence Army identity; no accepted employer match.
claims.temporal_assessment: No verified immediate employer or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Review Box 183 before decoding or linking any occupation to a named employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Catherine DeVaney may be Catherine Devaney Wallace, whose obituary reports OSS recruitment while she attended Rhode Island College.
claims.evidence_excerpt: She briefly attended Rhode Island College where she was recruited during World War II to work for the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An obituary independently supplies the uncommon indexed name and direct OSS recruitment context, but no Box 183, protected identifier, or personnel-file linkage.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high-confidence: the name and OSS service align, but no second person-specific identifier bridges the obituary to the index row.
claims.temporal_assessment: College attendance is described as preceding recruitment, not as employment. Two later-mentioned workplaces have no established pre-OSS dates.
claims.match_notes: Do not classify Rhode Island College as an employer or project the undated department-store and health-laboratory jobs backward. A separate 1958 college student of the same name is not assumed to be this wartime person.

claims.claim_text: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The possible obituary match establishes student status immediately before OSS recruitment, not a named pre-OSS employer; its two named jobs are undated.
claims.identity_match_assessment: A probable identity lead remains subject to Box 183 confirmation.
claims.temporal_assessment: Employment sequence cannot be established from the obituary.
claims.match_notes: Do not imply that Rhode Island College employed her or that either named job preceded OSS.

claims.claim_text: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A protected identifier leads to an official Army entry with the same forename and middle initial but a different surname spelling; accessible sources do not establish whether the two names identify one person.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous pending comparison with the indexed personnel file and original Army record.
claims.match_notes: Do not silently correct the printed surname or convert an Army occupation code to employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Hector F DeVega is a high-confidence match to Hector F De Vega in the official Army enlistment file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Full forename and middle initial match, the surname differs only by a space, and a protected identifier agrees across the two official records.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence orthographic variant plus direct private identifier agreement; the OSS personnel file has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Army entry predates wartime OSS service but does not name a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Preserve DeVega as indexed and De Vega as a documented search variant; full identifiers remain private.

claims.claim_text: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army record strengthens identity but gives no named employer; official discovery checks and exact-name employment searches yield no pre-OSS job citation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence Army identity, no accepted employer match.
claims.match_notes: Review Box 183 to identify any pre-OSS civilian workplace or transfer path.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The printed John and Sol Deull rows share a protected identifier and 'see also' notes; the official Army entry agrees with John's name. The two index rows are not merged without comparison of their Box 183 files.
person_updates.next_action: Compare the John B Deull and Sol Deull Box 183 personnel files to resolve the shared identifier and seek pre-OSS employer evidence.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The printed Sol and John Deull rows share a protected identifier and 'see also' notes; the official Army entry agrees with John's name, not Sol's. An alias, duplicate, or indexing error remains possible.
person_updates.next_action: Compare the Sol Deull and John B Deull Box 183 files before any merge or identity assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index row and official Army bulk file agree on the full name and a unique protected identifier. The Army occupation code is not a named employer.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 183 for William C Deutsch's civilian employer and military-to-OSS pathway; inspect any Army occupation code only with its official codebook.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The indexed Catherine DeVaney may be Catherine Devaney Wallace: a reviewed obituary independently reports that name and wartime OSS recruitment from Rhode Island College. It supplies no Box 183 or second identifier; two named workplaces have no pre-OSS dates.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 183 to confirm the obituary identity and date the department-store and city health-laboratory jobs before any employer assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index and official Army file share a protected identifier but differ in surname spelling; the potential De Vautour/Devautor variant requires file-level confirmation.
person_updates.next_action: Compare Box 183 with the official Army entry before resolving Francis A Devautor's identity or assigning an employer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index and official Army file agree on Hector F DeVega/De Vega and a unique protected identifier; the surname spacing is the only name difference. No named employer is supplied.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 183 for Hector F DeVega's pre-OSS civilian employer, if any, and military assignment pathway.
